stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
stages.hook: Say "mamá", "papá" and "casa". Can you hear five clear vowels?
explain: Spanish has five vowel sounds: a, e, i, o, u. They are short and clear, and they stay the same. The letter a always says /a/ as in "casa".
Most words are said just as they are written. The letter h is silent, so "hola" sounds like "ola". An accent mark, like in "mamá", shows which part to say loudly.
stages.mnemonic: A-E-I-O-U: five clean sounds, never changing.

gq.q: How many vowel sounds does Spanish have?
gq.why: Spanish has five clear vowel sounds.
The letter h is not pronounced in Spanish.

panel.q: Why does "papá" have an accent mark?
o: It shows the loud part is the last part
It means the word is plural
It shows it is a question
panel.why: The written accent marks stress on the final syllable here.

panel.q: Which word is said with the loud part on the first syllable?
panel.why: Casa is stressed on CA-sa; the other three carry an accent mark on the last syllable.

panel.q: How is Spanish spelling different from English spelling?
panel.model: Spanish spelling is much more regular: letters usually keep the same sound, so you can read a word aloud from its spelling.
panel.why: Spanish is largely phonetic.

teach.model: Spanish has five vowels: a, e, i, o, u. Each one has one clear sound. The letter h is silent. Most words are said as they are written.

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
stages.hook: Spanish has a letter ñ. How does it sound in "niño"?
explain: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters. It has the letter ñ (eñe), as in "niño" and "año". Until 2010 ch and ll counted as separate letters, but today they are not.
Each letter has a name: a (a), b (be), c (ce), d (de). The letter v and b sound the same in Spanish. The letter ñ sounds like "ny" in "canyon".
stages.mnemonic: Ñ wears a little wave on its head.
items: the letter n with a wave

gq.q: How many letters are in the modern Spanish alphabet?
gq.why: It has 26 Latin letters plus ñ, making 27.

gq.q: Which word has the letter ñ?
gq.why: Niño has ñ and means boy.

panel.q: Why does the word "año" differ in meaning from "ano"?
o: The ñ is a different letter from n
panel.why: Ñ is a separate letter; changing it changes the word.

panel.q: How do the Spanish letters b and v sound?
panel.model: In standard Spanish, b and v are pronounced the same.
panel.why: Both stand for /b/.

panel.q: Which letter is silent in Spanish words like "hermano"?
panel.why: H is never pronounced in standard Spanish.

teach.model: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters. It has one special letter, ñ. The letter h is silent. The letters b and v sound the same.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
stages.hook: How do you say hello and your name in Spanish?
explain: You can say "Hola" any time. In the morning say "Buenos días". In the afternoon say "Buenas tardes". At night say "Buenas noches".
To say your name use "Me llamo" and then your name. To ask a friend say "¿Cómo te llamas?" In Spanish, questions begin with ¿ and end with ?
stages.mnemonic: Hola, me llamo... Say it with a smile!

gq.q: Which greeting do you use at 9 in the morning?
gq.why: Buenos días is used in the morning.

gq.q: How does a Spanish question start?
gq.why: Spanish questions begin with an upside-down question mark.

panel.q: Why is "días" written with an accent?
o: To show that the stress is on í and the vowels are said separately
To show it is a question
panel.why: The accent on í breaks the pair i-a into two syllables: dí-as.

panel.q: Why does Spanish use ¿ at the start of questions?
panel.model: It tells the reader at the start of the sentence that a question is coming.
panel.why: Spanish punctuation marks both ends.

panel.q: Which reply fits "Mucho gusto"?
panel.why: Igualmente means likewise.

teach.model: Say Hola to greet someone. Say Me llamo plus your name. Ask ¿Cómo te llamas? Use Buenos días in the morning. Spanish questions start with ¿.

points.ask: How do I say my name?
How do I ask the name?

stages.title: Numbers and counting
stages.hook: Count your fingers in Spanish: uno, dos, tres... how far can you go?
explain: The numbers from one to ten are uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve and diez. Zero is cero.
Before a noun, uno becomes un or una: un libro, una casa. Dos and other numbers do not change: dos gatos, tres casas.
stages.mnemonic: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco: count with a hop!

gq.q: How do you say "one book" in Spanish?
gq.why: Libro is masculine, so we use un.

panel.q: How do you say "one house"?
panel.why: Casa is feminine, so we use una.

panel.q: Which number is written "ocho"?
panel.why: Ocho is eight.

panel.q: Why do we say "un" and "una" but not "uno" before a noun?
panel.model: Uno shortens to un before a masculine noun and changes to una before a feminine noun.
panel.why: Number one agrees with gender.

teach.model: Say the numbers: uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez. Before a noun, say un or una for one. Other numbers do not change.

points.ask: What happens with one before a noun?

stages.title: Colours and shapes
stages.hook: The sky is "azul" and grass is "verde". What colour is a banana?
explain: Colours: rojo (red), azul (blue), amarillo (yellow), verde (green), negro (black), blanco (white). In Spanish the colour comes after the noun: "el gato negro".
Colour words can change for gender: rojo is for masculine words and roja for feminine words: "un coche rojo", "una casa roja". Verde and azul stay the same.
stages.mnemonic: Noun first, colour second: gato negro.

gq.why: The colour goes after the noun and agrees with it: casa is feminine, so blanca.

gq.q: Which colour word does not change for gender?
gq.why: Verde ends in e and has one form.

panel.q: How do you say "a red car"?
panel.why: Coche is masculine, so we use rojo after the noun.

panel.q: What is "amarilla" describing in "la flor amarilla"?
panel.why: Flor is feminine, so the adjective ends in -a.

panel.q: Where does the colour word go in Spanish, and why does it change its ending?
panel.model: It goes after the noun and agrees with it in gender and number.
panel.why: Adjective agreement.

teach.model: Colours go after the noun: la casa blanca. Many colours change to match the noun: rojo for masculine, roja for feminine. Verde and azul stay the same.

stages.title: Family and people
stages.hook: Who is in your family? Say "mi mamá" and "mi hermano".
explain: Family words: madre (mother), padre (father), hermano (brother), hermana (sister), abuelo (grandfather), abuela (grandmother). In Spanish "mamá" and "papá" are used at home.
Nouns have gender. Words that end in -o are often masculine: hermano. Words that end in -a are often feminine: hermana. The plural "los padres" can mean the parents.
stages.mnemonic: -o for him, -a for her: hermano, hermana.

gq.why: The masculine plural can include grandfathers and grandmothers.

panel.q: Why do we say "mi hermana" and not "mi hermano" for a girl?
o: The ending -a shows a feminine word
panel.why: Gender is shown by the ending.

panel.q: What do "los hijos" mean?
panel.why: The masculine plural can refer to a mixed group.

panel.q: How do you make "hermano" refer to a female?
panel.why: Gender marking on nouns.

teach.model: Words for family change with gender: hermano for a boy, hermana for a girl. Words ending in -o are often masculine and words ending in -a are often feminine. Use mi before the word.

points.ask: How do I tell boy from girl?

stages.title: Common objects
stages.hook: In Spanish a table is "la mesa" and a book is "el libro". Why "la" and "el"?
explain: Every Spanish noun is masculine or feminine. The article shows it: el (masculine) and la (feminine). Many words that end in -o are masculine: el libro. Many words that end in -a are feminine: la mesa.
For plural use los and las, and add -s: los libros, las mesas. A or an is un (masc.) and una (fem.): un libro, una mesa.
stages.mnemonic: El is for -o words, la is for -a words.
sentences: The book is on the table.

gq.why: Add -s to a word ending in a vowel.

panel.q: What is the gender of "lápiz"?
panel.why: Lápiz is masculine, even though it does not end in -o.

panel.q: Which phrase is correct?
panel.why: Plural feminine nouns take las.

panel.q: Why must you learn the article with a new noun?
panel.model: The gender cannot always be predicted from the ending, and articles and adjectives must agree with it.
panel.why: Gender must be learnt with the noun.

teach.model: In Spanish every thing is masculine or feminine. Use el or la to show which: el libro, la mesa. For many things use los or las and add s.

points.ask: What kinds of nouns are there?
How do I talk about many?

stages.title: Everyday actions
stages.hook: What do you do every day? "Yo como", "yo juego", "yo leo"...
explain: Spanish verbs end in -ar, -er or -ir: hablar (to speak), comer (to eat), vivir (to live). To use a verb with "I", remove the ending and add -o: hablo, como, vivo.
With él or ella, add -a (for -ar verbs) or -e (for -er and -ir verbs): ella habla, él come, ella vive. The subject pronoun is often left out: "Hablo español."

gq.q: How do you say "I speak" in Spanish?

gq.why: For ella, an -er verb ends in -e.

panel.q: Why can Spanish say just "Vivo en Chile" without "yo"?
o: The verb ending already shows who is speaking
panel.why: Verb endings carry the person.

panel.q: What is the infinitive of "escribo"?
panel.why: The infinitive of the -o form escribo is escribir.

panel.q: How can you tell what person a Spanish verb is about?
panel.model: The verb ending changes with the person, so the ending tells you who does the action.
panel.why: Spanish is a pro-drop language.

teach.model: Spanish verbs end in -ar, -er or -ir. For I, take away the ending and add o: hablo. For he or she, use a or e. You can often drop yo.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
stages.hook: Someone says "¿Cómo estás?" What do you answer?
explain: A friend asks "¿Cómo estás?" (How are you?). You can answer "Estoy bien, gracias." If you do not understand, say "No entiendo" or "¿Puedes repetir, por favor?"
Listen for the question words: ¿qué? (what), ¿quién? (who), ¿dónde? (where). Speak slowly. Say "Más despacio, por favor" if someone talks too fast.
stages.mnemonic: Escucha, piensa, habla: listen, think, speak.
sentences: I do not understand the word.

gq.q: Someone says "Gracias". What do you answer?
gq.why: De nada means you are welcome.

panel.q: How do you ask a teacher to repeat politely?
panel.why: Puede (usted) is polite; por favor adds courtesy.

panel.q: Why do question words like "qué" and "dónde" have accents?
panel.model: The accent marks the question word and separates it from words like que (that) and donde (where, in statements).
panel.why: Written accent as a signal.

panel.q: Which phrase would you say when you step on someone's foot?
panel.why: Perdón is a quick apology.

teach.model: Listen first, then answer. For ¿Cómo estás? say Estoy bien. If you do not understand, say No entiendo. Ask them to say it again slowly with ¿Puedes repetir?

points.ask: What if I do not understand?
